assignments.why: Subject is typed decision models (Jev, Laya, Open-Jev); the contribution is a measurement (reassignment flip rates); decisions follow option names rather than bound definitions.
Audits the evidence on typed decision models across 28 papers, measuring baseline, saturation, calibration and cascade claims, and gives an evaluation checklist.
Benchmarks LLM user simulators with a User Fidelity Score on tau-bench-family agent tasks, showing the simulated user moves agent reward.

assignments.note: 2026-09 When the Right Answer Is Missing
assignments.why: Measures Jev's failure to reject menus with no correct answer even with a NONE option, and repairs it with a P(NONE) threshold.
Releases a 1.88B open typed decision model trained with cross-entropy plus Brier proper-scoring loss for calibrated distributions.
Compares outcome-only and step-level trajectory judges on injected faults in agent runs and proposes paired discrimination for trajectory scoring.

assignments.note: 2026-10 Adversarial Cues in Decision Models Used as Judges
assignments.why: Measures that a colon cue makes Jev as judge accept wrong answers only under sorted-key request serialisation, a logically equivalent presentation.
A meta-evaluation benchmark of agentic judges (coding-agent harnesses inspecting computer-use trajectories) on success vs near-miss pairs.
Tests a label-free method to improve LLM judges by rewriting the rubric clauses judges disagree on, an evaluator loop refining its own criteria from where judges split.
Releases LoRA-adapted open Qwen3.5 models that score candidates in one pass as a domain-specific Jev-style decision model.
Reliability audit of six frontier judges across repetitions, prompt formats and orders, finding order swaps flip most verdicts on hard tasks.
Builds a System One typed decision model for speech, trained on listener-vote distributions under a proper scoring rule for calibrated outputs.

assignments.note: 2026-10 Benchmarking Candidate Coverage and Rejection Policy Transfer
assignments.why: Benchmarks whether none-of-these rejection thresholds of Laya and Jev transfer across tasks and kinds of missing answers.
One harness compares decision models, LMs and classifiers on accuracy, calibration, name swaps and selective risk, and analyses when cascades to a second stage pay.
Controlled audit of whether Jev's calibrated confidence reflects missing knowledge, measuring calibration across knowledge levels and recalibration limits.
Steers LLM user simulators with calibrated user embeddings and argues simulators be judged by outcome calibration for multi-turn agent benchmarks.
Post-hoc multicalibration of a pairwise LLM judge to reduce bias across groups while improving accuracy.

assignments.note: 2026-10 Calibration and Risk-Budgeted Decisions with System One Models
assignments.why: Shows System One models' calibrated scores cannot be thresholded naively (low-score miscalibration) and certifies thresholds with Learn Then Test.
Audits eight typed decision models as judges against the CALM bias battery, with position bias as a main finding.
Fine-tunes small Qwen3.5 models with LoRA into an open Chinese single-pass decision model with a released deployment path.
Runoff, a training-free rule that makes System One decision models' choices invariant to option order.

assignments.note: 2026-10 Does a Hosted Decision Model Respect Irrelevant Alternatives
assignments.why: Pre-registered measurement showing Jev's option odds shift with the set of listed options (IIA violation).
Paired, self-audited comparison of LAYA and JEV at agent-harness decision points, including gates in front of an LLM and held-out threshold transfer.
Training-free compaction recipe (shared state, prefix trie, decision-guided layer pruning) for an open JEV model.
Fits a Bradley-Terry evaluator to Jev's pairwise probabilities, and averages two judges' probabilities to aggregate their labels.
Converts biomedical encoders into System One models and analyses the RLCD proper-score objective and temperature-scaled calibration.
Label-free recipe for a decision-model head on a frozen LM, also distilling a yes/no agent-run judge.
JEVal benchmark of where decision models replace LLMs, plus the open SII-Decision built by reasoning-to-readout self-distillation.
Releases a 0.8B-4B multimodal Jev-style decision model family trained with autoregressive masked LM.
Delegates agent steps to a decision model only above a fitted confidence threshold, else the LLM decides, and trains an open 4B decision model on agent states.
